why: a conditional expression reads its condition, then the selected operand only; a same-file call that changes its argument inside an operand changes it only when that operand is selected (design/heap-stage5.md section 3). The heap core reads both sides of note, route, stray, doubled and skewed (the world threaded through the arm taken): note returns the call from one operand where the candidate returns it from an if (proved); route is a nested ternary with the call in two operands against two ifs (proved); stray records at a non-positive count where the parent records nothing (unproved, WITNESS); doubled passes the ternary as an argument (proved); skewed records on both paths where the parent records only when the flag is off (unproved, WITNESS). The candidates of tally, ladder and leak assign in an if without a return, which the heap core does not read, so both sides take the value reading, where the arm taken carries the changed counter out: tally reads the counter after a ternary (proved); ladder passes a nested ternary as an argument (proved); leak changes the counter on both paths in the candidate (unproved, WITNESS); plain and the callees are untouched.
